items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of two critical PHP vulnerabilities enabling unauthenticated remote code execution, fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; PoCs are circulating.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: GitLab fixed a critical flaw allowing unauthenticated remote code execution on GitLab servers; CERT-EU urges prioritising internet-facing instances and compromise assessment.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: Cisco Secure Email Gateway AMP feature contains a critical flaw enabling unauthenticated remote code execution as root; active exploitation is confirmed and patches are available.

items.title: Joint statement on cyber incidents in refrigeration systems across the EU
items.summary: ENISA and partners issued a joint statement on cyber incidents affecting refrigeration systems across the EU, pointing to an OT/IoT supply-chain exposure.

items.title: Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches
items.summary: Zyxel patched a zero-day in GS1900 series switches exploited to compromise nearly 1,000 devices worldwide and steal configuration files and credentials.

items.title: French bank confirms cyber heist, hackers suspected to have stolen an estimated $133 million
items.summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed a cyber heist with an estimated USD 133 million stolen; attackers compromised an unnamed supplier and used the bank's own account for transfers.

items.title: Cyberattack disrupts blood storage refrigeration systems in France
items.summary: France's national blood service confirmed a cyberattack on a refrigeration equipment provider altered temperature and defrost settings at three facilities, endangering stored blood.

items.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root
items.summary: An APT package manager flaw in Debian and Ubuntu lets a man-in-the-middle swap verified packages during retried downloads and execute code as root; advisories published 4 November.

items.title: 2026. 11. 04. Kritikus Barracuda hibákkal root jogosultság szerezhető A Barracuda Networks két súlyos sérülékenységet javított hálózati biztonsági termékeiben, amelyek együttes kihasználásával akár t…
items.summary: Barracuda patched two severe flaws in its network security products that, chained together, can give attackers root privileges.

items.title: 2026. 11. 04. Az Apple kibertámadásokról küld figyelmeztetést a német politikusoknak A német Szövetségi Kiberbiztonsági Hivatal (BSI) hétvégén adott ki közleményt arra vonatkozóan, hogy politikusok é…
items.summary: Germany's BSI reports Apple threat notifications sent to German politicians and others, indicating targeted (likely state-linked) attacks on devices.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Patched Apple Flaw to Deliver Info-Stealing Malware, CISA Says
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2024-27834, an improper authentication flaw in Apple operating systems, to its KEV catalog after reports of exploitation to deliver info-stealing malware.

items.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
items.summary: Researchers found White House staff devices running residential proxy software that rents out their IP addresses, one service linked to a Russian operator.

items.title: OpenAI AI Pipeline Generates 948 Linux Root Escalation Exploits in 30-Hour Run
items.summary: OpenAI detailed an AI pipeline that reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and produced 948 local privilege escalation findings with patches for about USD 1.2m in API costs.

items.title: Critical Rails Bug Threatens to Derail Vulnerable Servers
items.summary: A critical Rails Active Storage/ImageMagick flaw lets attackers write arbitrary files and read sensitive data via uploaded images, enabling lateral movement.

items.title: More Asian airlines announce data breaches after attack on Spanish IT provider Amadeus
items.summary: Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Korean Air, Asiana, Singapore Airlines and Malaysia Airlines reported data breaches traced to an attack on Spanish IT provider Amadeus IT Group.

items.title: Tageszusammenfassung - 04.11.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily report covers the wave of attacks on refrigeration systems in Europe, now including Coolworld units storing blood supplies in France.

items.title: SonicWall Won't Patch EoL GMS Flaws That Could Expose Files, Alter Database Records
items.summary: SonicWall will not patch two flaws in end-of-life GMS 9.5.2 and earlier, including CVE-2026-109593 (CVSS 9.1) allowing unauthenticated file reads; migration is the only mitigation.

items.title: French bank Credit Mutuel Arkea counting losses from cyberattack
items.summary: Reuters reports Crédit Mutuel Arkéa is assessing losses from the cyberattack against it.

items.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
items.summary: OpenAI describes an autonomous pipeline that found, validated and patched 948 local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel.

items.title: 2026. 11. 04. Hamis állásinterjúval indult a Binance 6,3 milliárd dolláros kriptós támadása A Binance szerint észak-koreai hackerek egy látszólag ártalmatlan állásinterjún keresztül juttattak kártéko…
items.summary: Binance attributes a USD 6.3 billion crypto theft to North Korean actors who delivered malware via a fake job interview, a familiar social engineering playbook.

items.title: 2026. 11. 04. Több mint 200 sebezhetőséget javít az Android novemberi frissítőcsomagja A Google hétfőn új biztonsági frissítéseket adott ki az Android rendszerhez, amelyben több mint 200 sérülékenysé…
items.summary: Google's November Android security bulletin fixes more than 200 vulnerabilities; mobile fleets and BYOD devices should be updated promptly.

items.title: Investment scams with potential victims in at least 50 countries: over 100 servers seized
items.summary: German-led operation with Europol seized over 100 servers behind fraudulent trading sites used in investment scams across 50+ countries; seven suspects and EUR 4m+ in losses.

items.title: Healthcare can’t govern the AI tools it hasn’t found yet
items.summary: Survey finds 70% of healthcare leaders discovered AI-built tools handling patient data without IT or security awareness, highlighting shadow AI governance gaps.

items.title: Companies are spending more on AI governance and getting less control
items.summary: DNSFilter report: 74.5% of organisations raised security budgets, with AI security and governance the top spending priority, yet shadow AI control remains weak.

items.title: Most consumers aren’t ready to let AI agents shop unsupervised
items.summary: Okta report finds consumers hesitant to let AI agents transact autonomously, raising new requirements for verifying agents and managing their permissions.

items.title: Apple turns iCloud into spy cloud, will start looking at public share links
items.summary: Apple will begin scanning publicly shared iCloud links for 'harmful content', a term it has not defined, raising privacy and scope questions.

items.title: DreamHost confirms data breach exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
items.summary: DreamHost confirmed a breach in which attackers accessed its File Manager platform for two months and stole customer FTP/SFTP credentials and webmail sessions.

items.title: NIKKE PC game launcher hacked to spread remote access, data-stealing malware
items.summary: Attackers tampered with the PC launcher scripts of the game NIKKE in a supply-chain attack delivering credential- and crypto-wallet-stealing malware.

items.title: Neural data as the newest frontier in data privacy
items.summary: IAPP analysis on neural data emerging as a new frontier for data privacy regulation.

items.title: When does not using AI become negligence?
items.summary: Commentary exploring whether failing to adopt AI could become a form of professional negligence, with liability implications.

items.title: Democratic midterm wins set stage for tougher tech and AI scrutiny
items.summary: US midterm results shifting Congress to Democratic control are expected to bring tougher scrutiny of tech and AI companies.

items.title: Not a game: Europol and partners target terrorist role-playing online
items.summary: Europol's EU IRU and 16 countries ran a referral action day against violent extremist and terrorist role-playing content in online gaming environments.

items.title: BSI übergibt IT-Sicherheitszertifikate auf der it-sa 2026
items.summary: Germany's BSI handed over IT security certificates at the it-sa 2026 trade fair.

items.title: How to find a job in the age of AI
items.summary: Politico podcast on the European Commission's Education and Skills Package aimed at responding to AI's impact on Europe's labour market.

items.title: France braces for fresh protests as Macron seeks to prevent repeat of October unrest
items.summary: France prepares for renewed protests as the government seeks to avoid a repeat of October's unrest.

items.title: Zelenskyy hopes Democratic Congress will bring more US help for Ukraine
items.summary: Zelenskyy and EU officials hope the new US Congress will increase support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia.

items.title: Iran's IRGC says two tankers and tugboat caught fire in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's IRGC reports two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a key energy chokepoint.

items.title: Syria, Saudi Arabia sign defence cooperation deal, agree $403m in loans
items.summary: Syria and Saudi Arabia signed a defence cooperation agreement alongside USD 403 million in loans.

items.title: Canada spat exposes widening rift between Merz and von der Leyen
items.summary: A dispute over Canada's EU association status exposes growing friction between Berlin and Commission President von der Leyen.

items.title: Taiwan sees continued US arms sale support after midterm election
items.summary: Taiwan expects continued US arms sales support following the US midterm elections.

items.title: South Korea to expand anti-piracy unit operations closer to Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: South Korea will expand anti-piracy naval operations closer to the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: What Democratic control of Congress means for cybersecurity
items.summary: CyberScoop analysis of how Democratic control of the US Congress may reshape cybersecurity legislative priorities.

items.title: Officials extradite Canadian man to US for alleged cryptomining spree
items.summary: A Canadian man was extradited to the US over an alleged scheme hijacking university computing resources for cryptomining.

items.title: Canadian extradited to US for allegedly hacking schools in at least four states
items.summary: DOJ identified two suspects in a cryptomining intrusion campaign dating to 2016 against US educational institutions in at least four states.

items.title: Hugging Face’s CEO Says His P(Doom) Is ‘Close to Zero’
items.summary: Hugging Face CEO argues open-source AI reduces risk, saying most danger stems from closed development by a few major players.

items.title: Hungary releases secret police files from communist era
items.summary: Hungary released communist-era secret police files, revealing the names of the regime's informant network.

items.title: MEPs fear fundamental rights will take a hit under plans to expand EU border agency
items.summary: MEPs raise fundamental rights concerns over an expanded Frontex mandate that would support deportations to and from return hubs.

items.title: Midterms : 5 points que l’Europe doit surveiller après l’écrasante victoire des démocrates face à Trump
items.summary: Politico lists five consequences for Europe following the Democrats' sweeping US midterm victory.

items.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.
items.summary: OpenAI is acquiring Pierre Computer Company to expand Codex tooling for building, understanding and reviewing code.

items.title: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google
items.summary: UK's AI minister concedes the claimed GBP 400 billion economic benefit of AI, sourced largely from Google, is less than a third of that figure.

items.title: Daybreak Red is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East)
items.summary: OpenAI's Daybreak Red with GPT-5.6 Cyber is now available to approved customers via Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East).
